reason: Conversation 1 never engages with Er03 or the spill: it first misdiagnoses overheat protection, then when told pasta water hit the controls it issues an irrelevant 'water near the plug' stop-use warning and sends the homeowner to an electrician for a built-in hob, leaving the actual fix (wipe the slider, power cycle) undiscovered. Conversation 2 wrongly frames Er03 as moisture shorting the control electronics and speculates about 'permanent damage to the control PCB', and its 24-48 hour drying wait is wildly excessive for a touch panel that clears after 5 minutes, but its practical direction (isolate at the wall, dry, retry, test each zone) actually gets the homeowner to a working hob with no part or engineer. Neither names the real cause cleanly, but 2 resolves the problem while 1 escalates needlessly and leaves the customer stuck.
